sam: quick smoke: trying to repro a perf regression in the KV-evict path. want a tiny nsys capture that includes CUDA kernels + NVTX + OSRT. current one-liner I used:
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/kv-smoke --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --duration=3s ./bin/redwood-serve --workload=kv-evict-smoke
```
Any gotchas before I blow up disk with a 2GB file?

alex: for short captures I'd do 5s rather than 3s so you hit the slow path at least once. also bracket with NVTX so you can post-filter. e.g. emit NVTX around the request you care about and use --capture-range=nvtx for tight windows.

priya: ++ to NVTX bracketing. also use sample-mode to keep file sizes down if you don't need full tracing of every host thread. sample-based captures are way smaller and still show kernel hotspots.

mike: example NVTX bracket in runtime: 
```c
NVTX_PUSH("kv-evict-start");
... work ...
NVTX_POP();
```
Then: 
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/kv -t cuda,nvtx,osrt --capture-range=nvtx --capture-range-start "kv-evict-start" --capture-range-end "kv-evict-end" --duration=5s ./bin/redwood-serve ...
```
(adjust names per API).

sam: good call. I saw one run where attention_kqv kernel spiked to ~5ms and then a memcpy back-to-back. made me think batching heuristics changed. any tips for seeing memcopies easily?

alex: OSRT + CUDA timeline shows memcpy and kernel lanes. in the timeline, expand the PCIe/mem lanes. if you used sample mode you might miss tiny memcpy bursts — for those do a short full trace (no sampling) but only for NVTX-bracketed window.

priya: if you suspect kernel selection regression, capture a pair (good vs bad) and do a diff in the timeline: look for changed kernel names, different grid/block dims in the kernel tooltip, and shifts in queueing time before kernel launches. usually that points to a different kernel variant or changed token lengths affecting kernel selection.

mike: infra-bot FYI: disk quotas for /tmp on CI agents are 5GB. will drop artifacts older than 24h.

infra-bot: noted — large traces moved to s3://redwood-perf/archived if you pass -o /s3/... with upload hook.

sam: sweet. action items: 1) run NVTX-bracketed 5s full trace (no sampling) on one repro to capture memcpy+kernel, 2) run sample-mode short captures across a batch of requests to get distribution, 3) diff good vs bad timelines and paste snapshots here. i'll start with step 1 now.

alex: if you need a tiny command, here's a minimal full capture for a single bracketed request: 
```
# run server, trigger a single scoped request, then profile the NVTX range:
nsys profile -o /tmp/kv-full --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --capture-range=nvtx --capture-range-start "kv-evict-start" --capture-range-end "kv-evict-end" --sync-exit --duration=8s ./bin/redwood-serve 
```
--sync-exit helps ensure nsys waits for the capture to flush.

sam: thanks all, will upload the two traces when done. :thumbsup:
